title: Adoption of Northwind Analytics Cloud for analytics and dashboarding
context: Northwind Analytics Cloud is a vendor-hosted SaaS analytics and dashboarding platform with SAML federation, JDBC-based warehouse connectivity, a REST admin API, North America data storage, and JSON export of dashboards and dataset definitions. The conformance review shows multiple unresolved requirements across hosting, residency, identity, and integration controls.
standards_assessment: The submission conforms to some transport, encryption, and human-authentication requirements, but it also includes several findings that do not conform to mandatory standards. At least one non-conformance is structural and requires a design change rather than a contractual or procedural condition: the warehouse integration uses a direct JDBC-style connection between systems owned by different teams, which is not an approved integration pattern under STD-003 Section 1. Additional non-conformances include long-lived local service credentials and permanently assigned local administrator access. Because structural non-conformance is present, the appropriate decision is rejected.
decision_statement: Do not approve Northwind Analytics Cloud in its current design. The proposed solution must be redesigned to remove the prohibited JDBC-style direct integration and to address the remaining hosting, residency, identity, and operational gaps before resubmission.
decision_drivers: Vendor-hosted SaaS is only acceptable when all Section 3 conditions are met, and the submission does not fully evidence them.
Internal-classified data residency within the continental United States is not contractually guaranteed for backups, DR replicas, and support access.
The warehouse connection uses a direct JDBC-style integration between different teams, which is explicitly not approved.
Service-to-service authentication relies on a long-lived service account password rather than workload identity.
Administrative access is based on standing local administrator accounts rather than time-bound requested access.
positive_consequences: The review board has a clear basis to require redesign before adoption.
Rejecting the submission prevents approval of an integration pattern that conflicts with the approved standards.
A resubmission can focus on replacing the prohibited direct connector and closing the outstanding control gaps.
negative_consequences: The platform cannot be adopted as proposed.
The project will need redesign effort to replace the direct JDBC-style integration and rework privileged access and authentication.
Implementation timelines may be extended while the vendor and implementation team address the outstanding standard requirements.
